This morning was about Blueprints AI claiming permit-ready blueprints in minutes and shifting time away from drafting.

300+ hours saved per project, according to Blueprints AI.
4,000+ companies signed up, but that is demand, not proven production use.
ADU AI, from the same founder, sells a permit-ready package from $4,950 one time, while Blueprints AI was reported from $3,200 per month.

My take: in engineering, speed only matters if generation, review, and delivery fit the workflow people already run.

scenes: This morning, the post was about Blueprints AI saying it can generate permit-ready blueprints in minutes and update a full project from one change. I went back in to check the numbers around product scope, market pull, and what rivals already charge.
First, the company now puts a number on the pitch: 300 plus hours saved per project, with a first CD set in about 30 minutes of chat.
Second, Blueprints says more than 4,000 companies have signed up. That shows interest, but signed up is not the same as live inside an engineering workflow.
Third, the same founder’s ADU AI sells a permit-ready package at 4,950 dollars one time, while Blueprints AI was reported at 3,200 dollars a month.
My take: fast generation matters less than where the output lands. Simple, reviewable automation inside the real toolchain beats a smart-looking demo.
